statements.t: Looking forward, based on industry analyst projections, customer forecasts, cyclical demand, anticipated program launches and price changes, the Company expects revenues for calendar year 2026 to be flat to up 5% as compared to 2025.

The Company expects full-year 2026 gross margins to be approximately 16% to 17%, due to elevated freight, higher input costs due to oil prices and commissioning costs associated with the new Monterrey facility.

In addition, the Company expects to incur approximately $1.3 million of one-time costs related to relocating hood and battery production between U.S. facilities in the fourth quarter of 2026, impacting total Selling, General and Administrative expenses.
The Company anticipates spending approximat ely $28,000,000 to $30,000,000 d uring 2026 on property, plant and equipment purchases for all of the Compa ny's operations.
Included in the Company's anticipated spending in 2026 is approximately $18,000,000 to $20,000,000 for the Mexico expansion project.
The Company anticipates using cash from operations, its available revolving line of credit or its capex line to fund capital investments.

Monterrey is now operational, and the two 4,500-ton presses in Matamoros, which many of our investors saw under construction at our recent Investor Day, are on track to come online by year-end, further expanding our capacity and supporting long-term growth.

So far this year, we have secured approximately $30 million in new business awards and see a path to approximately $50 million in new business awards through six major projects currently in our last stage of our sales pipeline funnel.
Additionally, tooling project revenue accounted for a larger portion of sales during the quarter, which impacts our reported margins in the short term but creates recurring demand and revenue.
Consistent with our outlook discussed at our Investor Day, we continue to expect full-year net sales to be flat to up approximately 5% with gross margins in the 16% to 17% range.
The Company’s capital expenditures for the first nine months of 2026 were $19.7 million, including $12.2 million related to the Company's Mexico expansion project.
For the full year 2026, the Company expects capital spending of approximately $28 to $30 million, including approximately $20 million allocated to the Mexico expansion.

These statements are based on certain assumptions that the Company has made in light of its experience as well as its perspective on historical trends, current conditions, expected future developments and other factors it believes are appropriate under the circumstances.
